## Heat capacity, internal energy, enthalpy and entropy of each species (`cv_R`, `u0_R`, `s0_R`) {#sec-ch03-species-functions}

### Summary

Every mixture total of this chapter is a sum over species of a concentration times a molar function of temperature:
a heat capacity, an internal energy, an enthalpy or an entropy. This section gives those per-species functions.
Gases and condensates differ in three places: a gas has $c_p = c_v + \mathcal R$ and a condensate $c_p = c_v$; a
gas's enthalpy adds $z \mathcal R T$ to its internal energy; and a condensate's entropy is not read from data but
computed from the condition that each condensation reaction is in equilibrium on its saturation curve. The mixture
heat capacities are the concentration-weighted sums of these molar ones, per unit volume in J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$
(@eq-ch03-species-functions-mixture).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Molar $c_v$, $c_p$, $u$, $h$, $s$ per species, @eq-ch03-species-functions-u to
@eq-ch03-species-functions-scond.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], $c_n$ [mol m$^{-3}$] in; each function divided by $\mathcal R$ out.

**Placement.** Called by every `compute` conversion that returns an energy, an entropy or a heat capacity.

**Activation.** Always. Optional per-species extra functions; `use-nasa9-cp` and `use-h2-cp` replace $c_v$, $c_p$
and $u$ for the species they cover.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact closed forms; condensate entropy exact only for a full-rank nucleation block (Derivation).

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Symbols of the notation table (@sec-appa): $c^{\star}_n$, $u^{\star}_n$, $s^{\star}_n$, the YAML keys `cv_R` [-], `u0_R` [K] and
`s0_R` [-]; $c_{v,n}$ [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$], $u_n$, $h_n$ [J mol$^{-1}$], $s_n$ [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$], the molar
functions; $K_r$, saturation constant of reaction $r$ in Pa units; $T_\star$ [K], $p_\star$ [Pa], the reference state
of @sec-ch03-reference-state; $c_n$, $z_n$, $N_{\mathrm g}$ as in @sec-ch03-eos. Local symbols: $c_{p,n}$, molar heat
capacity at constant pressure [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; $\nu_{nr}$, stoichiometric coefficient of species $n$ in
reaction $r$, negative for a reactant [-].

### Derivation

**Internal energy and heat capacities.** With a constant heat-capacity coefficient, the molar internal energy that
equals $\mathcal R u^{\star}_n$ at $T_\star$ is

$$
\frac{u_n(T)}{\mathcal R} = u^{\star}_n + c^{\star}_n (T - T_\star) + e_n(T) ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-functions-u}

where $e_n(T)$ is an optional per-species extra function, zero unless C++ code registers one: no YAML key fills
an extra-function slot, `populate_thermo` pads them with empty names and the Python bindings do not expose them (verified by reading at the pin). @eq-ch03-species-functions-u is
computed in `eval_intEng_R` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_intEng_R >}}), with the constant
$u^{\star}_n - c^{\star}_n T_\star$ stored once as the offset at $T = 0$ (@sec-ch03-reference-state). Its
temperature derivative is the heat capacity at constant volume,

$$
\frac{c_{v,n}}{\mathcal R} = c^{\star}_n + \frac{\mathrm d e_n}{\mathrm d T} ,
$$

computed in `eval_cv_R` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_cv_R >}}), which calls the derivative of the extra
function under the name of the function with `_ddT` appended. For an ideal gas, $h = u + \mathcal R T$ gives
$c_p = c_v + \mathcal R$; a condensate has $c_p = c_v$. `eval_cp_R`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_cp_R >}}) adds 1 to $c^{\star}_n$ for the gases only, plus a separate
optional extra function for $c_p$.

**Mixture heat capacities.** The mixture values that the state modules return are sums over all species, gases and
condensates, of concentration times the molar value:

$$
\begin{aligned}
C_V &= \sum_n c_n\, c_{v,n}(T), \\
C_p &= \sum_n c_n\, c_{p,n}(T),
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-functions-mixture}

in J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$, since $c_n$ is in mol m$^{-3}$ and $c_{v,n}$, $c_{p,n}$ in J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. $C_V$ is the
`VT->cv` conversion of `ThermoY` (@sec-ch03-thermo-y) and $C_p$ the `TV->cp` conversion of `ThermoX`
(@sec-ch03-thermo-x). Per mole of mixture, divide by $\sum_n c_n$ (this is the $\bar c_p = \sum_n x_n c_{p,n}$ of the
adiabat, @sec-ch03-adiabat); per kilogram, divide by the density $\rho = \sum_n c_n \mu_n$ with $\mu_n$ the molar mass.
Because condensates have $c_{p,n} = c_{v,n}$, $C_p - C_V = \mathcal R \sum_{n < N_{\mathrm g}} c_n$ counts the gases
only (for $z_n = 1$ and no extra functions).

**Enthalpy.** For a gas the code writes $h_n = u_n + z_n \mathcal R T$, and for a condensate
$h_m = \mathcal R [u^{\star}_m + c^{\star}_m (T - T_\star)] + \mathcal R\, \zeta_m(T)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{h_n}{\mathcal R} &= \frac{u_n}{\mathcal R} + z_n T, \quad n < N_{\mathrm g}, \\
\frac{h_m}{\mathcal R} &= u^{\star}_m + c^{\star}_m (T - T_\star) + \zeta_m(T), \quad m \ge N_{\mathrm g} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-functions-h}

Here $\zeta_m$ is the condensate entry of the same `czh` function slot that holds $z_n$ for a gas; it is zero
unless set, so by default a condensate's enthalpy equals its internal energy (no $p v$ work for a phase of zero
volume). @eq-ch03-species-functions-h is computed in `eval_enthalpy_R`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_enthalpy_R >}}). The condensate line does not include the extra function
$e_m$ of @eq-ch03-species-functions-u (verified by reading `eval_enthalpy_R` at the pin).

**Gas entropy.** For an ideal gas with constant $c_p$, integrating $\mathrm d s = c_p\, \mathrm d T / T -
\mathcal R\, \mathrm d p_n / p_n$ from $(T_\star, p_\star)$ to $(T, p_n)$ with the partial pressure $p_n = x^{\mathrm
g}_n p$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{s_n}{\mathcal R} &= s^{\star}_n + \frac{c_{p,n}}{\mathcal R} \ln \frac{T}{T_\star} - \ln \frac{p}{p_\star}
- \ln x^{\mathrm g}_n + \sigma_n(T, p) , \\
x^{\mathrm g}_n &= \frac{c_n}{\sum_{k<N_{\mathrm g}} c_k} ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-functions-sgas}

where $x^{\mathrm g}_n$ is the mole fraction among gases only and $\sigma_n$ an optional extra function. The code
stores $s^{\star}_n - (c^{\star}_n + 1)\ln T_\star + \ln p_\star$ once and adds $(c^{\star}_n + 1) \ln T - \ln p$
with $T$ in K and $p$ in Pa. @eq-ch03-species-functions-sgas is computed in `eval_entropy_R`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_entropy_R overload=1 >}}). $x^{\mathrm g}_n$ is clamped at $10^{-300}$ before
the logarithm.

**Condensate entropy.** A condensation reaction $r$ is in equilibrium when its Gibbs energy change vanishes:

$$
\sum_n \nu_{nr} \left( h_n - T s_n \right) = 0 .
$$

Split the gas entropy into its pressure-free part $\tilde s_n$ and the partial-pressure term,
$s_n = \tilde s_n - \mathcal R \ln p_n$. At saturation the reaction quotient over the gases equals the saturation
constant, $\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} (-\nu_{nr}) \ln p_n = \ln K_r(T)$, with $p_n$ in Pa. The sum runs over every gas
of the reaction: gaseous reactants enter with positive exponents and gaseous products, which nucleation reactions
may have, with negative ones, so $K_r$ is a product of reactant partial pressures only when the reaction has no gas
product. Substituting and
dividing by $\mathcal R T$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 &= \sum_n \frac{\nu_{nr} h_n}{\mathcal R T} - \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \frac{\nu_{nr} \tilde s_n}{\mathcal R}
+ \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{nr} \ln p_n - \sum_{m \ge N_{\mathrm g}} \frac{\nu_{mr} s_m}{\mathcal R} , \\
\sum_{m \ge N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{mr} \frac{s_m}{\mathcal R} &= \sum_n \frac{\nu_{nr} h_n}{\mathcal R T}
- \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{nr} \frac{\tilde s_n}{\mathcal R} - \ln K_r(T) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-functions-scond}

Each nucleation reaction gives one such linear equation in the condensate entropies, with the left side
a row of the condensate block of $\nu_{nr}$. When each condensate is the product of exactly one nucleation reaction,
as for every cloud of `tests/jupiter.yaml`, each equation contains one condensate and gives its entropy directly:

$$
\frac{s_m}{\mathcal R} = \frac{1}{\nu_{mr}} \left[ \sum_n \frac{\nu_{nr} h_n}{\mathcal R T}
- \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{nr} \frac{\tilde s_n}{\mathcal R} - \ln K_r(T) \right] ,
\qquad r \text{ the reaction that forms } m .
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-functions-scond-one}

For one vapour condensing to one condensate this is $s_{\mathrm c} = s_{\mathrm v}(p_{\mathrm{sat}}) -
(h_{\mathrm v} - h_{\mathrm c})/T$: the entropy of condensation is the enthalpy latent heat over the temperature, the
statement of Clausius-Clapeyron. A condensate that has no nucleation reaction of its own but is a copy of another
condensate of the same phase, such as the precipitating `H2O(l,p)` made from `H2O(l)` by coagulation in
`tests/jupiter.yaml` with the same `cv_R` and `u0_R`, is the same substance: its entropy is its source's. The mixture
entropy is then $S = \sum_n c_n s_n$, over gases (with their mixing terms) and condensates.

Two things go wrong at the pin. First, the second `eval_entropy_R`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_entropy_R overload=2 >}}) solves all the equations at once with a Moore-Penrose
pseudo-inverse of the transposed condensate block. That reproduces @eq-ch03-species-functions-scond-one for a
condensate with its own reaction, but a condensate without one has a zero column and gets the minimum-norm value,
zero, instead of its source's entropy. When equations outnumber condensates the result is a least-squares fit rather
than a solution. That is the defect D64, whose fix gives a coagulation copy the entropy of its source
condensate.[^ch03-d64]
The reactions are the `type: nucleation` reactions only: the stoichiometry matrix is built from
`ThermoOptionsImpl::reactions` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_options.cpp ThermoOptionsImpl::reactions >}}). The data key
`s0_R` of a condensate is not used.

Second, the heat-capacity model has to be the same in $h_n$ and $s_n$. With `use-nasa9-cp` or `use-h2-cp` the gas
enthalpy and $c_p$ are T-dependent, so the gas entropy must be
$s_n/\mathcal R = \int c_{p,n}(T')/(\mathcal R T')\, \mathrm d T' - \ln(p_n/p_\star) + \text{const}$, which keeps the
Gibbs relation $T (\partial s_n/\partial T)_p = c_{p,n}$. At the pin the gas entropy keeps the constant
$c_{p,n} = \mathcal R (c^{\star}_n + 1)$ of @eq-ch03-species-functions-sgas while the enthalpy follows the option. That
is the defect K6, whose fix makes the gas entropy follow both options.[^ch03-k6] Because
@eq-ch03-species-functions-scond-one uses the code's own $h$ and $\tilde s$, the reaction Gibbs energy at saturation is
still zero at the pin; what is wrong is the vapour entropy itself.

The four energy-type functions are exact closed forms, and @eq-ch03-species-functions-scond-one is exact up to
round-off.

### Numerical method

Each function is evaluated pointwise over a tensor of cells, with the species as the last dimension. The optional
extra functions are dispatched per species through a tensor iterator (`call_func2`, `call_func3`), on CPU or CUDA.
At the pin the condensate entropies come from a pseudo-inverse of the condensate block, formed once per call from the
stoichiometry matrix and broadcast over the cells; for condensates that each have one reaction this is the direct
solve of @eq-ch03-species-functions-scond-one.

The species-function figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of the per-species functions. {#tbl-ch03-species-functions-code}

Walk-through. (1) `eval_intEng_R` adds the offset, $c^{\star}_n T$ and the extra function, then, when enabled,
replaces the entries of the NASA-9 species and of H$_2$. (2) `eval_cv_R` and `eval_cp_R` do the same for the heat
capacities. (3) `eval_enthalpy_R` builds on `eval_intEng_R` for gases only. (4) `eval_entropy_R` with the
`SpeciesThermo` argument returns gas entropies and zeros for condensates; with the `ThermoOptions` argument it also
solves @eq-ch03-species-functions-scond, which needs the reactions' saturation functions. Setup checks a user can
hit: both `eval_entropy_R` refuse a `conc` or `stoich` whose species dimension is not $N_{\mathrm g}$ plus the
number of condensates.

At the pin the NASA-9 and H$_2$ options replace $c_v$, $c_p$ and $u$ but not the gas entropy, which keeps the
constant $c_{p,n} = \mathcal R (c^{\star}_n + 1)$ of @eq-ch03-species-functions-sgas (K6).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_nasa9_cp.py` | with `use-nasa9-cp`, $c_p$, $c_v$ follow the polynomial | $10^{-10}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_nasa9_cp.py` | with it, finite-difference $\mathrm d u/\mathrm d T$ equals $c_v$ | $10^{-6}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_nasa9_cp.py` | NASA-9 and constant $u$ agree at 300 K | $10^{-12}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_nasa9_cp.py` | without it, $c_p/\mathcal R = c^{\star} + 1$, $c_v/\mathcal R = c^{\star}$ | $10^{-14}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_h2_cp.py` | H$_2$ $c_p$ in both modes against reference values | $2 \times 10^{-3}$ abs. | not yet derived |

: Tests of the per-species functions. {#tbl-ch03-species-functions-tests}

The tolerances are read from the test files at the pin.

The derivation is checked by `check_ch3_condensate_entropy.py`, with partial molar quantities at fixed $(T, p)$:
$h_n = \partial H/\partial c_n$ and $s_n = \partial S/\partial c_n$ (for the gases the mixing terms of the other species
cancel in that derivative).[^ch03-scond-check]

- `(e1)`: every nucleation reaction of `tests/jupiter.yaml` at a saturated state (`H2O(l)` at 250-300 K, `NH3(s)` at
  150-220 K, `NH4SH(s)` at 200 and 240 K): $\lvert \sum_n \nu_{nr}(h_n - T s_n)\rvert/(\mathcal R T)$ at most
  $3.4 \times 10^{-8}$ (tolerance $10^{-6}$, the central difference of $S$).
- `(e2)`: the copies `H2O(l,p)` and `NH3(s,p)` have $s/\mathcal R = 0$ at the pin, against $-9.342692$ and $-40.716115$
  for their sources, EXPECTED-FAIL (D64).
- `(e3)`: $T (\partial s/\partial T)_p = c_p$ for `H2O` gas at 250-900 K holds to $4.9 \times 10^{-11}$ with the flag
  off. With `use-nasa9-cp` the entropy still follows the constant 33.258 J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ while $c_p$ rises to
  40.0 J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at 900 K, a worst gap of 16.9%, EXPECTED-FAIL (K6).

`check_ch3_gibbs.py` adds a check away from saturation: moving H2O from vapour to liquid at fixed $(T, p)$ changes
$H - TS$ by $-\mathcal R T \ln \mathrm{RH}$ at four states with RH from 0.024 to 2.6, worst $3.9 \times 10^{-8}$ of
$\mathcal R T$. The mixture heat capacities of @eq-ch03-species-functions-mixture are checked by
`check_ch3_species_functions.py`: $C_p$ against a central difference of `TV->H` ($2.7 \times 10^{-11}$) and
$C_p - C_V = \mathcal R \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} c_n$ ($5.1 \times 10^{-16}$).

### Limits

At the pin, with `use-nasa9-cp` or `use-h2-cp`, the gas entropy keeps a constant $c_p$ while $u$, $h$ and $c_p$ do
not, so the vapour entropy fails the Gibbs relation by up to 16.9% at 900 K for H2O (check line `(e3)`, K6). The
condensate enthalpy ignores the extra internal-energy function.

At the pin every condensate without a nucleation reaction of its own has zero entropy (D64, check line `(e2)`). This
reaches `TPV->S` and `PVT->S`, `PXS->T` (@sec-ch03-thermo-x), and the rain-out target of the adiabat
(@sec-ch03-adiabat), which removes each condensate with its `eval_entropy_R` value. Moving condensate from a cloud to
its copy at fixed $(T, p)$ leaves $C_p$ and $H$ unchanged but changes $S$ by the cloud's $s_m$ times the moved
amount. Because $s_m$ depends on the arbitrary constants `s0_R`, `Tref`[^rg-3024f877ff0c] and
`Pref`[^rg-b6de325e7bca] (@sec-ch03-reference-state), so do the sign and size of that change.

The condensate entropy is the entropy of a constant-$c_p$ substance only when the condensate card matches its
saturation curve (@sec-ch03-reference-state, @eq-ch03-reference-state-sc-slope); the cards of `tests/jupiter.yaml` at
the pin do not (K8).

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-3024f877ff0c]: Tref — reference temperature in K; kinetics default 298.15 K, thermodynamics default 300 K; kinetics option `Tref`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0d9f67f97d841147e23283d2dcdab302238d2c45/src/kinetics/kinetics_options.cpp#L40-L41)

[^rg-b6de325e7bca]: Pref — reference pressure in Pa; kinetics and thermodynamics default 1e5 Pa; kinetics option `Pref`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/e357792d50639d68e9090b542edf038d2b029aa2/src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp#L62)
